title: Print the version with --version
body:
`tally --version` should print `tally 1.0.0` and exit 0. Nothing else changes.

---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

spec.plan: Before: `tally --version` is rejected by the flag set ("flag provided but not defined: -version", usage on stderr, exit 1). After: `tally --version` (and `-version`, which Go's flag package treats identically) prints exactly `tally 1.0.0` and a newline on stdout, writes nothing to stderr, and exits 0 without reading stdin or any file; every other invocation behaves exactly as today. Exact change in cmd/tally/main.go: (1) add a package-level `const version = "1.0.0"` with a one-sentence doc comment; (2) in `run`, register `showVersion := fs.Bool("version", false, "print the version and exit")` next to the existing `project` flag; (3) immediately after the successful `fs.Parse(args)` block and before the stdin/file selection, add `if *showVersion { fmt.Fprintln(stdout, "tally "+version); return 0 }` so it wins over any positional path and never blocks on stdin; (4) add the line `//	tally --version` to the usage examples in the package doc comment. No change to internal/tally (a version string is not timesheet logic), no new dependency, no ldflags/build-info machinery. Tests go in a NEW file cmd/tally/version_test.go (package main), so no existing test file is edited.
acceptance_checks: After `go build -o tally ./cmd/tally`, running `./tally --version; echo "exit=$?"` prints exactly two lines: `tally 1.0.0` then `exit=0`.
Running `./tally --version 2>/tmp/gh-aw/agent/err.txt >/dev/null; wc -c < /tmp/gh-aw/agent/err.txt` prints `0` — nothing is written to stderr.
Running `./tally -version` (single dash) prints `tally 1.0.0` and exits 0, the same as `--version`.
Running `sleep 10 | timeout 5 ./tally --version; echo "exit=$?"` prints `tally 1.0.0` then `exit=0` immediately, proving --version does not wait on stdin.
Running `printf '2026-11-20 site ninety\n' | ./tally --version; echo "exit=$?"` prints `tally 1.0.0` then `exit=0` — the timesheet is not parsed when --version is given.

Nothing else changes: `printf '2026-11-20 site 1h30m
2026-11-20 docs 45m
' | ./tally` still prints `site                 1h30m` then `docs                 0h45m` and exits 0, and `printf '2026-11-20 site 1h30m
2026-11-20 docs 45m
' | ./tally --project docs` still prints only `docs                 0h45m`.
`go vet ./... && go test ./...` passes, and `gofmt -l .` prints nothing.
tests_added: cmd/tally/version_test.go: TestRunWithVersionFlagPrintsTheVersionAndExitsZero — calls run([]string{"--version"}, strings.NewReader("2026-11-20 site ninety\n"), &stdout, &stderr) and asserts code == 0, stdout == "tally 1.0.0\n", stderr == "" (the malformed stdin proves the timesheet is not read), using t.Fatalf with the actual values interpolated as main_test.go does.

cmd/tally/version_test.go: TestRunWithVersionFlagIgnoresAMissingFile — calls run([]string{"--version", "/nope.txt"}, strings.NewReader(""), &stdout, &stderr) and asserts code == 0 and stdout == "tally 1.0.0\n", proving --version is answered before any file is opened.

research.claim: cmd/tally/main.go already parses arguments with a flag.FlagSet in ContinueOnError mode (the `--project` flag) inside a testable `run(args, stdin, stdout, stderr) int`; an unknown flag currently returns 1. A `version` bool flag fits this existing pattern with no new surface type.

Go's flag package accepts `--version`, `-version` and `--version=true` identically for a Bool flag; flags after the first positional argument are not parsed (`x --version` leaves version false), which is existing flag behaviour and not changed by this plan.
research.source: ran: in /tmp/gh-aw/agent/exp a FlagSet with fs.Bool("version",...) run via `go run main.go --version`, `-version`, `--version=true x`, `x --version` printed true,true,true,false

research.claim: Go flag syntax: one or two dashes are equivalent; boolean flags may be given without a value.

Existing cmd tests are in cmd/tally/main_test.go and call run() with bytes.Buffer stdout/stderr and strings.NewReader stdin, asserting with t.Fatalf and sentence-style names; the new test file follows the same shape so main_test.go is not edited.

Logic about timesheet content belongs in internal/tally and main stays thin; output goes to stdout, diagnostics to stderr, failure exits non-zero. A version string is wiring, not timesheet logic, so it stays in cmd/tally.
Changing cmd/tally/main.go requires tests alongside it: the coverage gate requires 80% diff coverage and the manifest instruments cmd/tally with -coverpkg=./...
The sandbox can build the binary, run it on stdin/arguments, read stdout/stderr and exit status, and run go vet/go test/gofmt — every acceptance check is one of these.
product_work may change code and tests only; cmd/tally/ is not a protected path and no practices are recorded that bear on this change.
